pr_title: [JS] Some functions (print, alert,...) must be called only after a user activation
pr_body:
- Some events, which require a user interaction, will allow those functions to be called. But after few seconds, if there are no more user interaction, it won't be possible anymore.
The idea is to give an opportunity to the user to leave the pdf.
- Disable print function when we're printing, the same with saving and disallow to save on open events.

Close #15614.

issue_context.title: Save and print loops in PDF viewer with JS in PDF.
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: Chrome Versie 106.0.5249.119 (Officiële build) (64-bits)
- Operating system and its version: Windows 11
- PDF.js version: https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html
- Is a browser extension: No

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1.  Use a pdf with this javascript in it: /JS (app.setInterval('app.execMenuItem("SaveAs")', 1000);)
2.  Use a pdf with this javascript in it: /JS (app.setInterval('print()', 100);)
3.  Use a pdf with this javascript in it:  /JS (app.setInterval('app.alert("123")', 1);)

File 1. [test.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/9852207/test.pdf)
File 2. [test.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/9852212/test.pdf)
File 3. [test.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/9853150/test.pdf)


Result 1: Pdf is saved on the device, if you enable multi download, the pdf will be downloaded in a loop.
Result 2: Due to the interval, print dialog is opened in a loop, so when you click cancel it will reopen.
Result 3: Alert will show in a loop,
comments: The "Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:"-part of the ISSUE_TEMPLATE is required in order for any issue to be actionable/valid, and please always fill out the ISSUE_TEMPLATE with *all* of the requested information.

Those kind of actions (`print`, `alert`, ...) should be triggered only after a user activation.
Adding a check for a user activation will at least help to break the loop and then let the user decide to leave the pdf without being annoyed by a modal.
The first file completely breaks Firefox ESR 102.3.0 on Debian with the build in PDF viewer.
For the 1st one, you just have to wait few seconds and then cancel the print, to get rid of the print call.

review_comments: Don't we need similar code in the `"Print"` case below?
Also for zoom maybe? I saw you also added code for `set zoom(value)`?

There are no zoom events after having triggered a zoom so it doesn't make sense.
FYI, save/print trigger a `Will***` and `Did***`, and I'm just disabling save/print when the associated callback are called because those events aren't trigger by the user themselves (and because it doesn't make sense, but I can change my opinion if someone has a good example).

Given that saving is listed in the `dontRun` Set above, why do we need to explicitly disable saving here?

---

If this actually is necessary, a comment would probably be a good idea.
Furthermore, if this is intended, why don't we set `disablePrinting` here as well?

Because it'll disable auto-print.
